texts: bad: the clause carries two verbs, and 'at dawn' — which belongs to the returning — was copied onto the carrying as well, so the parse asserts a dawn time for the carrying that your sentence never states. Move the time into the opening frame, which does legitimately cover both verbs: "At dawn on day 34 of Year 1, the harvest party returned to Cauldron Hall and carried twelve full buckets of salt-bloom." Two smaller notes that need no rewrite: the buckets-to-salt-bloom link is improvised (there is no licensed form for a container 'of'), and 'day 34 of Year 1' stores as a bare day number beside a year rather than as a well-formed date.
good. the harvest is typed and 'heavy' is asserted of it under past tense — nothing more.
good. Hesper is the agent, the salt-bloom carried in the buckets is the same symbol here (so the passage tracks one batch), the store is its destination, and the store's 'store' genus is unpacked.

good. 'each compartment' becomes a per-compartment rule — every compartment of the store gets its own past writing event with Hesper as agent, the date as what was written and that compartment as the place — and the rule is fireable, so any compartment named later picks up its own entry.
good. 'stayed potent' is recorded as a continuing state of that same salt-bloom: the state, the continuation marker, past tense, and the plain 'was potent' atom for direct questions.
